title: Universal-cone presentations of the relative fibred Cech nerve
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], and a morphism $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal X$ over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ of categories fibred in groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Use the big etale topology, abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], common-target tuple category $A_p(f)$, compatible-family term $T_a=\operatorname{Ran}_{a^{op}}\circ a^*$, and coefficient-transport pullback of [def-sfb-fibred-relative-cech-complex]. A presentation of the relative Cech nerve consists, in every degree $p\geq0$, of a category $P_p$ and a universal cone functor $q_p:P_p\to A_p(f)$. Universality means that $q_p$ is full, faithful and essentially surjective: the leaf objects, common root and comparison isomorphisms represent every cone up to isomorphism, and every compatible arrow of cones lifts uniquely. This is the cone form of the iterated $(p+1)$-fold 2-fibre-product universal property and permits any bracketing and representative; for $p=0$ it permits $\mathcal U$ with its cone $(u,f(u),1)$, as well as $A_0(f)$. For $0\leq j\leq p+1$ there is an omission functor $d_j:P_{p+1}\to P_p$ and a specified natural isomorphism $q_pd_j\cong\partial_jq_{p+1}$ of cone functors, where $\partial_j$ deletes leaf $j$. Thus the comparison includes the leaf and root data, not just an equivalence of categories without its cone.

Put $a_p=\operatorname{root}\circ q_p$, $E^{-1}_P(F)=F$, and $E^p_P(F)=T_{a_p}(F)$. The augmentation is the restriction/right-Kan-extension unit; each coface is compatible-family pullback along $d_j$ with the root isomorphism of the specified cone comparison, and the differential is their alternating sum. The common-target presentation has $P_p=A_p(f)$ and $q_p=1$, with strict deletion faces. Restriction of compatible families along $q_p$ defines the canonical map $\rho^p:E^p_A\to E^p_P$; put $\rho^{-1}=1$. Terms and maps are functorial in the abelian coefficient, and are first defined in presheaves, restricting the coefficient to sheaves. Given the differential-square-zero equations, form the cochain complex by these terms in indices $n=p+1\geq0$ and extend by zero along $n\mapsto -1+n$ to integer degrees. When these terms are sheaves, the full sheaf inclusion identifies this construction with the complex of abelian sheaves.
